auth_scheme: OAuth2 client_credentials against login.microsoftonline.com -> Bearer token to graph.microsoft.com/.default scope
install_tell: LiteLLM guardrail_hooks/microsoft_purview uses Graph API user-resolve + Purview DLP policy evaluation; tenant_id, client_id, client_secret are mandatory; user-id resolution chain (LiteLLM user_id -> end_user_id -> metadata) is the impersonation-risk surface called out in source comments
misconfig_patterns: Caller-influenceable user_id resolution (end_user_id, metadata user_api_key_*) is impersonation surface; trusted-id mode strips caller-supplied keys but operator must opt in.
Service principal client_secret leakage hands attacker Graph API access scoped to the Purview application registration; scope of damage depends on Graph permissions granted at consent time.

active_probe.notes: Microsoft public Graph endpoint; identity-fingerprint only

deployment_tells: Purview DLP runs in customer Azure tenant; only public surface is graph.microsoft.com (same as all M365)
No vendor-specific Shodan surface; cert-pivot covers all Graph API consumers, not Purview specifically
